Computation time

Source: vignettes/articles/simFastBOIN-speed.Rmd
simFastBOIN-speed.Rmd

The simulation engines of the package are written in C++. This article gives the time that each design takes to simulate the trials of one scenario and to summarize their operating characteristics, on one machine. The times are read from inst/benchmark/results/benchmark.csv, written by inst/benchmark/benchmark.R.

What is measured

The 11 designs that were compared with a reference implementation, in another R package or in the code of the authors of the design, are run by both with the same settings and the same number of trials: those of the comparison of the design in inst/validation/ or inst/reproduce/, or of the README for the BOIN design, with the number of trials used there for the reference. TITE-gBOIN-ET is timed against two references, ‘boinet’ and the R program of the supporting information of Takeda et al. (2023), a script that runs all the settings of the article and that is run here as published for one of them, with its own rules, which differ from those of the package in the two points described in the article “How the package is checked”. The 10 other designs are run by the package alone, with the settings of the example in their vignette and 10,000 trials. The settings are listed in the section “Settings” below.

The time is the elapsed time of one call. A fast call is repeated until the repetitions take at least one second, and the time per call is kept. Every time was measured 3 times, alternating between the two implementations, and the tables give the median. Printed output and warnings of the calls are discarded. The package was installed before it was timed: devtools::load_all() compiles the C++ code without optimization.

The machine

The times were measured on 2026-11-27 under Windows 11 x64 (build 26200), on an Intel(R) Core(TM) Ultra 7 155H with 16 physical cores, with R 4.6.1. The simulations of the package run on one core. The code of the authors of BOIN-ETC (the GitHub repository kakizume/BOINETC) and the program of Takeda et al. (2023) have no version; the versions of the packages were

Package Version
simFastBOIN 2.3.0
BOIN 2.7.2
boinet 1.6.0
bfboinet 1.1.0
UnifiedDoseFinding 0.1.10
escalation 0.2.3

Designs compared with a reference implementation

Design Trials Reference Reference (s) simFastBOIN simFastBOIN (s) Times faster
BOIN 10,000 BOIN::get.oc() 8 sim_boin() 0.031 260
BOIN combination 1,000 BOIN::get.oc.comb() 0.53 sim_comb_boin() 0.067 7.9
Waterfall 500 BOIN::get.oc.comb(mtd.contour = TRUE) 1.4 sim_waterfall() 0.05 29
BOIN-ET 5,000 boinet::boinet() 18 sim_boin_et() 0.038 480
TITE-BOIN-ET 2,000 boinet::tite.boinet() 48 sim_tite_boin_et() 0.047 1,000
gBOIN-ET 5,000 boinet::gboinet() 22 sim_gboin_et() 0.12 190
TITE-gBOIN-ET 5,000 boinet::tite.gboinet() 140 sim_tite_gboin_et() 0.35 400
TITE-gBOIN-ET, program of the article 1,000 simulation1_TITE-gBOIN-ET.R of Takeda et al. (2023) 23 sim_tite_gboin_et() 0.085 270
BF-BOIN-ET 1,000 bfboinet::get.oc.backboinet() 280 sim_bf_boin_et() 0.026 11,000
gBOIN 4,000 UnifiedDoseFinding::get_oc_QuasiBOIN() 8 sim_gboin() 0.033 240
BOIN12 2,000 escalation::simulate_trials() 120 sim_boin12() 0.031 3,900
BOIN-ETC 1,000 get.oc.BOINETC() of Kakizume et al. (2024) 0.41 sim_boin_etc() 0.015 28

The package was between 7.9 and 11,000 times faster than the reference implementation. The ratio is smallest for the three drug-combination designs: 7.9 for the BOIN drug-combination design, 29 for the waterfall design and 28 for BOIN-ETC. For the first two, both packages select the MTD of every trial with the bivariate isotonic regression of Iso::biviso(), called from R once per trial. The code of the authors of BOIN-ETC simulates the trials and writes them to a file, and selects the optimal dose combinations afterwards with another function, CALC.SUM(), which is not timed; the package does both. The ratio is largest for BF-BOIN-ET, whose reference implementation takes 280 seconds for 1,000 trials.

Other designs

Design Trials simFastBOIN Seconds
iBOIN 10,000 sim_iboin() 0.04
Accelerated BOIN 10,000 sim_boin() 0.028
TITE-BOIN, imputation 10,000 sim_tite_boin() 0.078
TITE-BOIN, ESS 10,000 sim_tite_boin() 0.066
BF-BOIN 10,000 sim_bf_boin() 0.16
BE-BOIN 10,000 sim_be_boin() 0.17
TITE-BOIN12 10,000 sim_tite_boin12() 0.79
U-BOIN 10,000 sim_uboin() 0.19
Comb-BOIN12 10,000 sim_comb_boin12() 78
TITE-Comb-BOIN12 10,000 sim_tite_comb_boin12() 77

Other implementations exist for some of these designs, such as the ‘TITEgBOIN’ package for TITE-BOIN, but they were not compared with the package and are not timed here. 8 of the 10 designs take less than one second for 10,000 trials. Comb-BOIN12 and TITE-Comb-BOIN12 take about 78 and 77 seconds: by default (est_method = "logistic") they estimate the response probabilities at the end of every trial by the posterior mean under the logistic model of Lu et al. (2025), computed by importance sampling with 4,000 points (n_draws = 4000). With est_method = "observed", the observed response rates, the selection is much faster.

The scripts named in the settings are in inst/validation/ and inst/reproduce/, from which the scenarios of the articles are also taken.

Measuring on your own machine

From the root of the source package, install the package, restart R and run

library(simFastBOIN)
source("inst/benchmark/benchmark.R")
res <- run_benchmark(boinetc_zip = "path/to/BOINETC-main.zip",
                     takeda2023_zip = "path/to/Takeda_2023_SI.zip")

with the reference packages ‘BOIN’, ‘boinet’, ‘bfboinet’, ‘UnifiedDoseFinding’ and ‘escalation’ installed and the zip files of the code of the authors of BOIN-ETC and of the supporting information of Takeda et al. (2023); a design whose reference is missing is recorded as such. The run writes inst/benchmark/results/benchmark.csv. Most of the time goes to the reference packages.

References

Kakizume, T., Takeda, K., Taguri, M. and Morita, S. (2024). BOIN-ETC: A Bayesian optimal interval design considering efficacy and toxicity to identify the optimal dose combinations. Statistical Methods in Medical Research, 33(4), 716-727.

Lu, M., Zhang, J., Yuan, Y. and Lin, R. (2025). Comb-BOIN12: A utility-based Bayesian optimal interval design for dose optimization in cancer drug-combination trials. Statistics in Biopharmaceutical Research, 17(2), 266-276.

Takeda, K., Yamaguchi, Y., Taguri, M. and Morita, S. (2023). TITE-gBOIN-ET: Time-to-event generalized Bayesian optimal interval design to accelerate dose-finding accounting for ordinal graded efficacy and toxicity outcomes. Biometrical Journal, 65(7), 2200265.
